recognize_zh: CD79a 免疫染色：大量小 B 淋巴球呈強陽性，而夾雜其中細胞質淡染的大型漿母細胞樣細胞為陰性或僅弱染；大細胞缺乏 B 細胞抗原（CD20、CD79a），與 HHV8 陽性漿母細胞表型相符，支持 germinotropic LPD。
features: Strong CD79a staining of numerous densely packed small B lymphocytes
Scattered and clustered large cells with abundant pale cytoplasm are negative to weak
Negative large cells appear as pale islands within the positive small-cell background
Some large cells show faint cytoplasmic blush only
describe_en: Immunohistochemical stain for CD79a shows strong staining of the numerous small B lymphocytes, while the admixed large cells with abundant pale cytoplasm are negative or at most weakly stained, forming pale islands within the positive background. The distribution of negative large cells mirrors that seen on CD20. Absence of CD79a and CD20 in the large cells indicates a plasmablastic phenotype that has lost B-cell program markers. In conjunction with HHV8 LANA-1 and EBER positivity, the findings support HHV8-positive germinotropic lymphoproliferative disorder.

ddx.vs: Plasmablastic lymphoma cells are often CD79a positive (weak) with CD20 negativity, form effacing sheets and are HHV8 negative.
MCD plasmablasts are cytoplasmic IgM-lambda positive, scattered in mantle zones and EBV negative.
HRS cells are usually CD79a negative too, but they are CD30+/CD15+ with weak PAX5 and lie in a mixed inflammatory background without HHV8.
